minVersion.description: Lowest protocol version accepted by the gateway.

maxVersion.description: Highest protocol version accepted by the gateway.

nonce.description: Single-handshake challenge value to return unchanged when authenticating.

expiresAt.description: Challenge deadline as Unix seconds, rounded up from millisecond wall time. The server enforces one monotonic timeout including challenge delivery; expiry closes with retryable handshake_timeout.

SessionChallenge.description: Server challenge received before authentication. The SDK checks version overlap, then returns the nonce with credential evidence; callers normally use NessaClient.connect instead of building this payload.

id.description: Identifier of the connecting client application or instance.

ProductClientMetadata.description: Caller identification sent during the product handshake. This metadata does not grant permissions.

ProductSurfaceKind.description: Kind of user-facing surface. The same closed set as protocol/schemas/v1/common.json SurfaceKind; generation refuses a drift. Metadata only: it does not grant permissions.

instance.description: Identifier distinguishing instances of this surface.

ProductSurface.description: Surface the handshake names so the gateway can tell connections that share a credential apart. The credential still decides identity.

minVersion.description: Lowest protocol version supported by this client.

maxVersion.description: Highest protocol version supported by this client.

nonce.description: Nonce from the current SessionChallenge; a reconnect obtains a new one.

credential.description: Opaque secret credential evidence. Send only during authentication; do not log it.

client.description: Descriptive client metadata, separate from authenticated identity.

surface.description: Surface kind and instance. Descriptive only; the credential decides the principal.

SessionAuthenticateParams.description: Wire request for session.authenticate. NessaClient.connect builds this after validating the server challenge; a successful response is ProductSessionReady.

principalId.description: Authenticated human, integration, agent, or paired peer gateway identity.

organizationId.description: Organization in which this session operates.

membershipId.description: Membership connecting the principal to this organization.

credentialId.description: Credential used to authenticate this connection.

audienceId.description: Gateway audience to which the credential is bound.

expiresAt.description: Exclusive Unix seconds, or null for no expiry.

grants.description: Current credential restrictions; not permanent authorization.

methods.description: Registered product methods; permission is checked for every command.

ProductSessionReady.description: Authenticated connection snapshot returned by the product handshake and auth.session(). Links the principal, organization membership, credential, and gateway. It describes current restrictions; the server checks current authorization again for every command.

kind.description: Category of actor; this alone does not grant access.

ProductPrincipal.description: Identity that acts in the product: a human, integration, agent, or paired peer gateway. A principal needs an active organization membership and an appropriate credential to access the gateway.

role.description: Organization role evaluated by authorization policy.

state.description: Whether the membership is active or disabled.

ProductMembership.description: Relationship between a principal and an organization. The role participates in authorization and disabled membership prevents access.

organizationId.description: Organization owning the resource; must match the credential organization.

id.description: Resource identifier, such as the gateway ID for server operations.

ProductResource.description: Organization-scoped authorization target used by ProductGrant. The gateway resolves the actual resource for each operation before checking policy.

action.description: Authorization action, for example server.read. This is a policy action rather than an RPC method name such as server.health.

resource.description: Exact organization-scoped target on which this action is requested.

ProductGrant.description:
One action/resource restriction on a credential. Used in credential issuance, credential metadata, and authenticated session snapshots. A grant is not a standalone permission: current membership and server policy must also allow the operation.

For example, { action: "server.read", resource: { organizationId: "personal", id: "gateway" } } scopes server-read access to that gateway; use the actual organization and gateway identifiers from your installation.

id.description: Identifier used to revoke this credential.

organizationId.description: Organization in which the credential applies.

audienceId.description: Gateway audience allowed to accept this credential.

expiresAt.description: Exclusive Unix seconds, or null for no expiry.

revokedAt.description: Revocation time in Unix seconds, or null if not revoked.

grants.description: Action/resource restrictions evaluated along with current server policy.

ProductCredentialMetadata.description: Non-secret description of a credential returned by issue and list operations. Describes who it authenticates, its gateway audience, lifetime, and grant restrictions; it cannot itself authenticate a connection.

requestId.description: Idempotency key identifying this issuance operation.

principal.description: Identity the new credential will authenticate.

membership.description: Organization membership associated with that principal.

expiresAt.description: Exclusive Unix seconds, or null for no expiry.

grants.description: Requested action/resource restrictions; at least one is required.

CredentialIssueParams.description: Wire input for issuing a scoped credential. Prefer client.credentials.issue, whose IssueCredentialParams allows the SDK to generate requestId. Reuse the same ID and inputs when explicitly retrying an uncertain result.

CredentialListParams.description: Empty wire input for credential.list. The SDK list() method supplies this object.

requestId.description: Idempotency key to reuse for retries of this revocation.

credentialId.description: Identifier of the credential to revoke.

CredentialRevokeParams.description: Wire input for credential.revoke. Prefer client.credentials.revoke to generate and preserve the request ID.

credential.description: Non-secret metadata for the issued credential.

secret.description: One-time credential evidence accepted by product connect auth. It is not replayed on a duplicate request.

IssuedCredentialResult.description: First successful issuance response. Contains secret evidence only once; keep it in private storage before discarding the result.

credential.description: Metadata for the previously issued credential.

secretUnavailable.description: Always true: this response does not contain a usable secret.

ExistingCredentialResult.description: Response when the issuance request ID already completed. Metadata is returned, but the original secret cannot be recovered by retrying.

credentials.description: Non-secret credential records returned by the gateway.

CredentialListResult.description: Credentials visible to the authorized caller, without secret evidence.

revision.description: Authorization-state revision returned by the mutation.

SessionCloseReason.description: Product session termination reasons used to determine whether connection recovery is allowed. Revocation, expiry, authorization loss, and incompatible protocols are terminal; transient transport and gateway failures may retry.

PrincipalKind.description: Supported categories of authenticated actors: human users, integrations, agents, and paired peer gateways. Only device pairing creates a gateway principal; credential.issue refuses one.

MembershipRole.description: Organization roles understood by product authorization policy.

MembershipState.description: Membership availability. Disabled membership prevents access even when credential evidence is valid.

code.description: Product reason corresponding to the WebSocket close code.

retryable.description: Whether the reason permits connection recovery; cannot override numeric-code policy.

retryAfterMs.description: Optional server delay hint in milliseconds, bounded to 60,000.

SessionTermination.description: Structured WebSocket close reason. The SDK derives retry policy from the numeric close code and accepts matching, bounded server delay hints.

ConversationMessageStatus.description: Current invocation status, including unresolved interrupted history.

ConversationPendingMode.description: How an admitted input waits for dispatch.

ConversationDisposition.description: How the gateway accepted or recovered this submission.

ConversationLifecyclePhase.description: Current provider attachment state. This is presentation state and grants no operation authority.

ConversationStartupFailureCode.description: Stable category for a provider attachment failure.

ConversationStartupFailure.description: Bounded presentation of the latest provider attachment failure. It carries no admission or cleanup authority.

message.description: Bounded diagnostic suitable for display, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes. `x-utf8MaxBytes` is the authoritative byte bound; `maxLength` is a coarse code-point bound.

ConversationAttachmentEvidenceFailure.description: Bounded late failure to acknowledge mandatory attachment audit evidence. It carries no lifecycle authority.

code.description: Mandatory attachment audit was not acknowledged.

message.description: Bounded diagnostic suitable for display, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes. `x-utf8MaxBytes` is the authoritative byte bound; `maxLength` is a coarse code-point bound.

ConversationLifecycle.description: Current provider attachment lifecycle for this conversation.

failure.description: Present exactly when phase is failed.

evidenceFailure.description: Late mandatory attachment-audit failure retained independently of the current phase. It grants no lifecycle authority.

PermissionDenialSupport.description: Whether Nessa can deliver a deny choice offered by a provider permission review.

NativeHookSuppressionSupport.description: Whether suppression of user-configured provider hooks has been verified.

NativeHooksChoice.description: Whether this launch allows the harness's own hooks. Off asks the harness to leave them off. On means hooks can approve, deny, or change a tool call and its result without Nessa asking, and can run commands when the agent starts. On does not prove a hook ran, and it does not change nativeHookSuppression.

NativeHooksAgent.description: A harness whose own hooks the caller can allow. OpenCode is not in this set and stays suppressed.

CompactionReportingSupport.description: Whether Nessa reports provider compaction with invocation correlation.

ModelSwitchReportingSupport.description: Whether Nessa reports a provider model switch after validation.

PermissionDeferralSupport.description: Whether a review can be deferred for a later answer. unsupported means this provider cannot defer. unsupported_not_implemented means Nessa has not built deferral for a provider that might.

ElicitationForwardingSupport.description: Whether the provider binding forwards one correlated elicitation round trip.

PreToolPolicySupport.description: Whether a configured Nessa policy can deny a tool held at a permission gate.

PolicyEndTurnSupport.description: Whether a Nessa policy can end its correlated current invocation.

PolicyCloseSessionSupport.description: Whether a Nessa policy can close its correlated provider session.

IncomingElicitationSupport.description: Whether the negotiated agent can ask and receive a correlated answer through Nessa.

ConversationAgentFeatures.description: Scoped provider transport facts and effective Nessa policy integration support.

permissionDenial.description: Scoped delivery support for a rejecting option offered by a provider review.

nativeHookSuppression.description: Verified suppression state for user-configured provider hooks.

nativeHooks.description: The hooks choice this conversation was started with. When on, hooks can approve, deny, or change a tool call and its result without Nessa asking, and can run commands when the agent starts. For Claude, on also applies the repo's .claude settings, including its allow rules and startup hooks.

compactionReporting.description: Effective Nessa support for correlated compaction reporting.

modelSwitchReporting.description: Effective Nessa support for validated model-switch reporting.

permissionDeferral.description: Effective Nessa support for an explicit nonterminal permission defer outcome.

elicitationForwarding.description: Provider forwarding support for a correlated elicitation round trip.

preToolPolicy.description: Effective Nessa support for enforcing configured policy before a held tool runs.

policyEndTurn.description: Effective Nessa support for ending a current invocation from policy.

policyCloseSession.description: Effective Nessa support for closing a provider session from policy.

incomingElicitation.description: Effective Nessa support for receiving and resolving incoming elicitation.

ConversationCapabilities.description: Operations supported by this configured agent.

queue.description: Can queue input at invocation boundaries.

imageInput.description: The connected agent advertised image input. False until an agent has been opened, and whenever it advertised none.

agentFeatures.description: Scoped transport and effective application support for agent features.

ImageAttachment.description: One uploaded image a message refers to. The bytes travel on the upload path, never in a socket message.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the image bytes: `sha256:` and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

size.description: Image length in bytes, at most 5 MiB.

LinkedFile.description: One file a message points the agent at. The gateway, the agent and the panel run on one machine, so the path travels and the bytes never do; the agent opens the file itself, with the reader's approval, or does not open it at all.

path.description: Absolute path on the machine the gateway runs on, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes (`x-utf8MaxBytes`; the `maxLength` beside it counts code points and is only a coarse upper bound, since a path within the byte limit always has fewer code points than bytes). Every component below the root is a name: no control character (C0 or C1), none empty, and none `.` or `..`. A component that is empty or a dot does not survive being written as a URI, which would make the link name a different path; a control character makes a path nobody can be shown before they approve the read. Nothing here is a rule about markdown — the gateway hands the path to the agent inside a link and encodes both halves of it down to an allowlist, so a bracket or a backslash in a name is the encoder's business and not the caller's.

AttachmentBeginParams.description: Ask to upload one file into a conversation. Repeating it for bytes the conversation already holds needs no upload.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the bytes to be uploaded; the upload is refused unless the received bytes hash to it.

mimeType.description: Declared lowercase media type without parameters. Storage accepts any; what a message may refer to is narrower.

size.description: Exact length in bytes, at most 64 MiB, which admits a camera RAW file; the upload is refused unless it is exactly this long.

ArtifactReadParams.description: Read one range of a file a conversation holds: an artifact its agent published, or an image uploaded into it. Name the file exactly as the conversation's view does. A surface reads the whole file range by range and checks its size and digest itself.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the held file, as the view names it.

mimeType.description: Media type the file is held as, as the view names it. The same bytes held as another type are another file.

size.description: Exact length of the held file in bytes.

offset.description: First byte of the range; less than size.

maxBytes.description: Most bytes to answer with. The answer carries fewer only at the end of the file.

ArtifactReadResult.description: One range of the held file. Nothing in it is verified: assemble the ranges, then check the whole against the file's size and digest before showing or keeping it.

offset.description: First byte of this range, as asked.

data.description: The range's bytes, standard base64 with padding: at most maxBytes, and fewer only when the file ends first.

AttachmentBeginResult.description: Either the conversation already holds this upload, with the reference a message uses for it, or a single-use ticket to upload it. A successful `PUT /attachments` answers with the same reference shape.

requestId.description: The action this answers.

state.description: `stored` needs nothing further; `upload_required` carries a ticket.

ticket.description: Secret single-use upload ticket, sent as the `x-nessa-upload-ticket` header of one `PUT /attachments`. Null when stored. Do not log it.

expiresAtMs.description: Unix milliseconds after which the ticket is refused. Null when stored.

digest.description: When stored: digest of what the conversation holds, which is what a message refers to. The gateway may have converted or compressed the upload, so this can differ from the uploaded digest. Null when an upload is required.

mimeType.description: When stored: media type of what the conversation holds. Null when an upload is required.

size.description: When stored: length in bytes of what the conversation holds. Null when an upload is required.

ConversationUsageLimit.description: A provider usage limit on a failed turn. resetsAtMs is present only for a timed reset whose instant parsed. autoResuming is present only when this gateway has accepted a one-shot continuation for the turn.

provider.description: The harness that reported the limit. OpenCode is not a value.

recovery.description: How the limit can end. timed_reset carries resetsAtMs. user_action needs the person and never carries a reset. unknown is a usage limit with no trustworthy reset.

resetsAtMs.description: Absolute Unix milliseconds when a timed reset ends, kept only inside 2024-01-01 through 2100-01-01 UTC.

autoResuming.description: True only when a continuation for this turn is scheduled or being delivered and the gateway preference is on.

ConversationMessage.description: One bounded conversation turn; omitted older text is indicated by the enclosing truncated flag.

executionId.description: Stable invocation identifier retained for retries of one logical message, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

userText.description: User input text; empty for a message of images alone.

attachments.description: Images the user sent with this turn, in attachment order.

files.description: Files the user pointed this turn at, in attachment order. No bytes were ever carried for them.

app.description: The app that wrote this turn on the person's behalf; absent when the person wrote it.

authenticationRequired.description: The provider adapter explicitly requires authentication for this failed turn. Generic provider codes and diagnostic text do not establish this fact.

requiredWorkFailed.description: This failed turn also failed independent required work, beside an authentication refusal or a usage limit. The person-facing diagnostic stays in error. Absent for a pure refusal or a pure usage limit.

usageLimit.description: A provider usage limit on this failed turn. Absent when the turn did not end in one. autoResuming is present only after a continuation has been scheduled.

steeringTarget.description: Execution that consumed this injected steering input; its shared reply answers this input.

parts.description: Provider observations in execution order; offsets address the retained SDK event sequence.

steeringOffset.description: Target event count when steering was admitted locally; does not imply provider consumption timing.

ConversationPending.description: A waiting input that may be removed before dispatch.

executionId.description: Stable invocation identifier retained for retries of one logical message, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

text.description: Waiting user input; empty for a message of images alone.

attachments.description: Images waiting with this input, in attachment order.

files.description: Files the waiting input points at, in attachment order.

app.description: The app that wrote this waiting input on the person's behalf; absent when the person wrote it.

ConversationMessageApp.description: The MCP App that wrote a turn on the person's behalf (mcp.sendMessage): the tool call whose UI it is, and the MCP server and tool that call was to.

executionId.description: The execution the app's tool call belongs to.

tool.description: The tool whose UI the app is.

ConversationPermissionOption.description: An exact option offered by the provider.

effect.description: What choosing this option decides for the reviewed request, as the gateway's domain classified the provider's offer: allow it, or deny it. A surface picks an option by this, never by its label or identifier.

ConversationPermissionOptionEffect.description: Whether a permission option allows or denies the reviewed request. Only options that decide that one request are offered: the gateway offers no review with a choice that reaches further.

ConversationPermissionDeadline.description: What happens if nobody answers this review, and when. Absent on a review that waits for a person.

waitMs.description: How many milliseconds the review waits before this outcome is taken, measured when the review was armed.

dueAtMs.description: Unix milliseconds on the gateway's clock when the deadline decides. A reloaded client counts down from this rather than starting waitMs again, measured from the view's serverNowMs rather than its own clock.

effect.description: The outcome taken when the wait ends with no answer.

reason.description: Past-tense reason recorded if the deadline wins: not blank, and free of control characters. A pending review does not show this sentence; it builds a line from the outcome and the wait.

stopsTurn.description: True when the only refusal this agent offered stops the turn; never true for an allow. The pending line and the notice say that, rather than that the turn continues without the tool.

ConversationPermission.description: A pending review with all it shows, as conversation.permissionReview reads it for one entry of a view.

review.description: The key the view lists it under. An answer names it, so a review whose identities are reused is never answered by mistake.

executionId.description: Stable invocation identifier retained for retries of one logical message, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

options.description: Complete offered choices; never silently shortened.

origin.description: Who asked for this review: the agent or an MCP App.

ask.description: What the review asks the person to allow.

argumentsJson.description: The reviewed input, exactly as the agent or the app gave it.

deadline.description: Present when the review answers itself if nobody does. Absent for a review that waits for a person, including an app review.

ConversationReviewEntry.description: One review waiting on a person, as a view lists it: its key, who asked, and the start of the tool's name. A view never leaves one out for its size. Read what it shows with conversation.permissionReview, and offer no answer until that has loaded.

review.description: The review's own key: new for every review opened, so a review whose identities are reused is a new entry.

origin.description: Who asked: the agent, or an MCP App.

toolName.description: The start of the reviewed tool's name, to say what the review is while the rest is read.

ConversationQuestionEntry.description: One question waiting on a person, as a view lists it: its key and the start of the agent's message. A view never leaves one out for its size. Read all it asks with conversation.questionReview, and offer no answer until that has loaded.

question.description: The question's own key: new for every question asked, so a question whose identities are reused is a new entry.

message.description: The start of the agent's message, to say what the question is while the rest is read.

ConversationTool.description: Bounded presentation of an observed tool call.

executionId.description: Stable invocation identifier retained for retries of one logical message, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

toolId.description: Tool call identity within the execution.

kind.description: What the call does, as the provider categorised it. Empty until the provider has said, which is why a panel counts kinds it knows rather than assuming the rest are reads.

details.description: Bounded provider-observed tool output and file changes; omitted content is marked.

input.description: The call's input, one JSON object encoded: the arguments the agent reported with the call, or those its permission request asked with, whichever came last and fit. Empty when none was reported or none fit — never cut.

mcp.description: The MCP server and tool the call went to, as the agent's harness named them (Claude's harness replaces characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] in a tool name with _); absent for a harness's own tools and where the harness does not say which server.

structuredContent.description: The call's structured result (MCP structuredContent) as JSON text, when the harness passed it on and it fits; absent otherwise. The result's text stays in details either way.

nativeHooks.description: The hooks choice of the process start this tool call ran under, saved with the call so it survives a gateway restart. Absent when that start recorded none: a harness without the choice, or a call saved before it was recorded. Recorded input and output are what the model proposed or the tool returned, and a hook may have changed or approved them when this is on.

startedAtMs.description: When the gateway first heard of the call, in Unix milliseconds, saved with the call so it survives a restart. Absent for a call saved before the time was recorded.

endedAtMs.description: When the gateway heard the call completed or failed, in Unix milliseconds. Absent while the call runs, for a call that never settled, and for a call saved before the time was recorded.

changes.description: The files the call changed, as the agent reported them and in its order, at most 16. The same changes are written into details as text; these are for a reader that draws them, and the first a view gives up for room, before any turn. Absent when the call reported none.

changesCut.description: The call changed files changes does not list: more than 16, one whose path is past its bound, or the list was given up for room. A reader totalling changes knows the total is not the call's. Absent when changes lists every file the call reported.

ConversationToolChange.description: One file a tool call changed: its path, and its text before and after.

path.description: The file's path as the agent named it, unresolved. A change to a file whose path is longer than 4096 bytes is not listed, and changesCut says so.

before.description: The text before the change, cut past 7000 bytes. Absent when the agent did not say — a file it created reads that way — which differs from an empty file.

after.description: The text after the change, which may be empty, cut past 7000 bytes.

cut.description: A side was longer than 7000 bytes and is cut, so the two sides do not say the whole change.

ConversationMcpTool.description: An MCP tool's identity: the server by the name it was configured under, and the tool on it; the UI the tool declared, when known; and the arguments the gateway's connection saw for the call, when it could match them.

server.description: The MCP server's configured name. Which names are valid is the SDK domain's rule (McpTool); only its byte bound is repeated here, generated for both sides.

tool.description: The tool's name on that server, under the same rule.

resourceUri.description: The ui:// resource of the tool's MCP App, as the gateway's own connection to the server last listed the tool (no harness passes it through ACP); absent when the tool declared none or it is not known. Which URIs are valid is the SDK domain's rule (UiResourceUri); only its byte bound is repeated here.

argumentsJson.description: The call's arguments, one JSON object encoded, as the gateway's MCP connection saw them. The same bound as a review and an app's own call (maxMcpArgumentsBytes). Absent when the call did not go through that connection, the harness named no call id it could match, or the arguments did not fit — never cut.

ConversationView.description: Bounded full replacement of the current live conversation view. Polling never implies cancellation or durable streaming storage.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

revision.description: Opaque revision; compare for equality, never numeric ordering.

serverNowMs.description: The gateway's Unix milliseconds when it made this view. A client measures each deadline's dueAtMs against this, not against its own clock, so a clock on another machine that is ahead or behind does not move the countdown.

messages.description: Recent turns with current streamed output.

permissions.description: Every review waiting on a person now, oldest first: the agent's (the SDK holds at most MAX_OPEN_REVIEWS open) and then the MCP Apps'. Each entry is small and of fixed size, and a bounded view gives up everything else before any of them, so none is ever left out.

truncated.description: Some history, text or whole interactions were omitted to bound this response; interactionViewError explains omitted actionable units.

interactionViewError.description: Why complete pending reviews or questions cannot safely be shown; do not infer omitted choices or question fields.

queueComplete.description: All currently pending execution IDs are represented, so an exact reorder may be attempted.

transcriptState.description: Committed physical transcript completeness and freshness, independent of display truncation.

runtime.description: Configured provider, model and working directory for this conversation.

lease.description: The conversation's latest lease: where its agent runs and under what limits, or why it could not. Absent before any lease was recorded.

artifacts.description: Files its agent published under a lease that the conversation held when it recorded them, the newest 64 in the order they were recorded; empty before any was. A record is history and stays when the hold is let go, as closing the conversation does; whether the bytes are still held is asked when they are fetched. An older one is left out of the list, not out of the conversation, and the list may give up its oldest entries to bound the response.

notes.description: Notes left in the conversation (conversation.message), the newest 64 in the order they were left; empty before any was. An older one is left out of the list, not out of the conversation, and the list may give up its oldest entries to bound the response.

handoffs.description: Switches to another agent or model, and the fork the conversation began as, in the order they were recorded; empty before any.

unreadable.description: Records this read could not apply, oldest first, at most 32. Empty when every record could be read. A chat with no turns may still list these. Each is one line in the transcript. The line is where a future report action attaches; this view carries no report control.

unreadableTruncated.description: True when more records could not be read than the 32 lines in unreadable. Those records were still skipped. The transcript ends with one line: More parts of this conversation couldn't be read.

title.description: Name the gateway derived from the conversation's first message, or the one a person renamed it to, the same one conversation.list shows; null before anything was said.

questions.description: Every question the agent is waiting on now, oldest first (the SDK holds at most MAX_OPEN_QUESTIONS open). Each entry is small and of fixed size, and a bounded view gives up everything else before any of them, so none is ever left out.

approvalModeChange.description: Present while a change is in progress or recovery is required.

modelChange.description: Pending correlated model change; the confirmed selection remains authoritative.

usageLimitAutoContinue.description: Whether this gateway schedules one continuation when a usage limit resets. The preference is the gateway's, shared by every conversation, and defaults to false. The card copies Auto-resuming only when a schedule for that turn has been accepted.

modelChangeEffect.description: Native effect boundary of the last confirmed model change.

model.description: The conversation's selected catalog model, present whether or not an agent is open.

ConversationArtifact.description: One file its agent published under a lease: read from the environment, verified by its digest, held, and then recorded with the lease as its cause. The record outlives the hold. The bytes are never in the view.

executionId.description: The turn that was running when it was recorded; absent when none was.

lease.description: The lease it was published under. Which identities are valid is the SDK domain's rule (LeaseId); only its byte bound is repeated here.

name.description: The file name it was published under, for people only: it names no place on any machine. Which names are valid is the SDK's rule (ArtifactName: no `/` and no control character); only its byte bound is repeated here.

digest.description: SHA-256 of its bytes: `sha256:` and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

mimeType.description: The media type it was declared as, lowercase without parameters. Which types are valid is the SDK domain's rule (MediaType); only its byte bound is repeated here.

size.description: Its length in bytes, at most 64 MiB.

ConversationCreateParams.description: Idempotently create or reopen one named conversation.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

agent.description: Coding agent this conversation runs on for its whole life. Omitted takes the gateway's configured default. Ignored when the conversation already exists, which is reopened on the agent it was created with.

model.description: Initial catalog model identifier; ignored on reopen. Use conversation.setModel to change an existing chat.

approvalMode.description: Initial preset, default ask; ignored on reopen.

environment.description: Where this conversation's agent runs for its whole life: one of the environments agents.list returns, an SSH destination, a paired environment's peer: name, or peer:any, any worker of the gateway's pool, which the gateway chooses each time the agent is opened. Omitted runs it on the gateway's own machine. Ignored when the conversation already exists, which keeps the environment it was created with.

channelId.description: The channel the conversation is in for its whole life, one channel.list returns: its agent works in that channel's folder and is told the channel's notes and resources. Omitted, or default, is the default channel, whose folder is the gateway's configured workspace. A channel other than default runs on the gateway's own machine, so it is refused invalid_request beside an environment. channel_not_found when the caller has no such channel. Ignored when the conversation already exists, which stays in the channel it was created in.

ConversationCreateResult.description: Conversation ready for read and admission.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

ConversationPeekResult.description: Capture the locally active execution without opening a provider. Null means no active execution; bounded transcript views are not used to select it.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.
Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

ConversationDeleteParams.description: Delete a conversation permanently: stop it, ask its agent to delete the agent's own session, record who deleted it, and erase its history, uploads and summary. Audit evidence is retained. The identity is never reused: its owner's later commands on it answer conversation_deleted, except deleting it again, and anyone else is told conversation_not_found. A repeat of the deciding request — the same principal, surface and requestId — is answered applied true, any other delete by its owner applied false; either repeat first carries on an erasure that has not finished. conversation_erasure_incomplete and audit_unavailable mean the conversation is deleted and its erasure did not finish; deleting again, and each gateway start, tries again. Any other error from a delete means only that it is not known whether the conversation was deleted: list it, or delete again.

ConversationCapability.description: One capability a conversation grant may include. read: list, read and follow the conversation's records. comment: leave notes with conversation.message and ask where its own note stands with conversation.messageStatus. drive: start, steer and stop turns, answer or cancel their permission requests, answer their questions and look up those commands' receipts (conversation.send, steer, stop, answer, answerQuestion, cancel, receipt), with text only and under the grant's constraints. The only sets are read; read and comment; and read, comment and drive. Comment and drive are refused for a gateway principal. No capability deletes, archives, exports, re-shares or changes the model: those stay the owner's.

ConversationToolPreset.description: A named tool policy. read_only_tools: only tools that read. no_shell: every tool except shell commands. ask_everything: every tool, each one asked for. all: every tool, asked as the conversation's approval mode asks.

ConversationToolPolicy.description: The tool policy a drive grant's turns run under: either preset alone, or allow and deny together. Allow and deny each hold at most 16 patterns, and at least one of the two holds one (both empty is refused); each pattern is 1 to 48 UTF-8 bytes with no surrounding whitespace and no control character; anything else is refused invalid_request. A pattern's * matches any run of characters and every other character is itself; a pattern matches a tool's name as the agent or the gateway names it (Read, read, run), and a deny wins over an allow. Every tool call a drive turn's agent asks permission for, and the gateway's own run, artifacts_publish and artifacts_fetch, is checked against the policy at the revision the turn was admitted under; a refused call is answered as refused and the turn goes on. An allowed run goes only to a host commandHosts names and the gateway grants commands on, and runs only a program the gateway allows. One thing a policy does not limit: what the agent does in the ask approval mode without asking (Claude reads files; Codex runs commands in its read-only, offline sandbox), so a deny pattern naming a read tool does not stop those reads.

preset.description: A named policy. Present alone, without allow or deny.

allow.description: Tools the holder's turns may call. Present with deny, without preset.

deny.description: Tools the holder's turns may never call. Present with allow, without preset.

commandHosts.description: The hosts the holder's turns may run commands on with run, by the name environments_list gives them: an SSH destination or a paired environment's peer: name, never here, each named once and at most 253 bytes, the longest destination config.json accepts. Beside either preset or allow and deny, and not counted against the patterns: a policy may name 16 hosts however full its allow and deny lists are. A host is used only where the gateway also grants commands on it. Absent or empty, the holder's turns run commands nowhere: a drive grant never inherits the owner's hosts. A host that is no such name, one named twice, one longer than 253 bytes, or more than 16 is refused invalid_request. Listed only when it names a host.

ConversationShareParams.description: Grant (conversation.share) one paired device or peer gateway a capability set on one of the caller's conversations, or change the capabilities and constraints it already holds there. Nothing is granted by default or by list: a paired party sees only the conversations granted to it, one grant per conversation, and an ungranted one is not listed, not readable and cannot be followed. The only sets are read; read and comment; and read, comment and drive. drive needs a policy and the others take none, and either mistake is refused invalid_request. Comment and drive are written only when Cedar permits grant.comment and grant.drive for the target principal. A denial writes nothing and is refused capabilities_refused; details.policies are the Cedar policy ids, empty when no permit matched. The share does not decide by the principal's kind. A grant is refused share_target_not_paired unless the credential is an active paired device or peer gateway of the conversation's owner that holds conversation.read (an environment's credential never does), and conversation_deleted on a deleted conversation. The result names the grant's policyRevision, the grant epoch, once the share is made; applied is false when nothing changed: granting the capabilities and constraints already held, whose epoch is kept. With expectedPolicyRevision, a grant that is no longer at that epoch (changed or revoked since) is refused share_grant_changed, and nothing is changed. A conversation holds at most 64 grants, and at most 8 drive grants; one more is refused invalid_request. A retried requestId answers what it answered the first time, its policyRevision included, before expectedPolicyRevision is compared, so a share retried after a later unshare grants nothing; the same requestId naming another device, another capability set or policy, or the other change is refused invalid_request. A retried share is checked like a new one first, so once the conversation is deleted or the device unpaired it is refused conversation_deleted or share_target_not_paired and changes nothing.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

credentialId.description: The paired device's credential, as credential.list names it.

capabilities.description: The capabilities to grant, in any order. read; or read and comment; or read, comment and drive.

policy.description: The constraints: the tool policy. Present exactly when capabilities includes drive.

expectedPolicyRevision.description: The policyRevision of the grant this change was made from, as conversation.shares or an earlier share's result named it. When given, the change is made only while the device's grant is still at that revision, decided in the same transaction that writes it; otherwise it is refused share_grant_changed and nothing is changed. 0 names no grant held (revisions start at 1): a first grant built on a list without one is refused once another lands. Absent, the change is made whatever the device holds.

ConversationUnshareParams.description: Revoke (conversation.unshare) one paired party's grant on one of the caller's conversations, whatever its capabilities. A revoke needs only ownership, so it works on a deleted conversation and for a party since unpaired. Revoking ends the party's next read; a read already admitted may finish. applied is false when no grant was held. Either way the party holds no grant afterwards, so the result names no revision: the revoked grant's row is gone, and a later grant takes an epoch of its own. With expectedPolicyRevision, a grant that is no longer at that epoch (changed or revoked since) is refused share_grant_changed, and nothing is changed. A retried requestId answers what it answered the first time; the same requestId naming another device or the other change is refused invalid_request.

Absent, the change is made whatever the device holds.

pageSize.description: How many grants this page may hold, from 1 through the published page size. A page of that many grants, each at its largest, fits one frame.

credentialId.description: The paired device's credential, as credential.list names it.

A later page belongs to the same read only when it names the same revision. A conversation holds at most 64 grants; one page holds at most its page size.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.
