items.description: Stable invocation identifier retained for retries of one logical message, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

executionIds.description: Exact desired full waiting order, including steering inputs. Running invocations are excluded.

ConversationReorderOutcome.description: Applied or unchanged order, or a rejected stale queue/steering-priority conflict. Rejections leave the queue unchanged.

ConversationReorderResult.description: Acknowledgement of one atomic queue reorder control.

requestId.description: Identity of this deliberate control action; an uncertain acknowledgement requires a fresh read, not replay.

outcome.description: Whether the whole requested order was accepted.

ConversationLease.description: The conversation's latest lease as its records fold. A lease is the recorded permission for one environment to run this conversation's agent with named limits; every run of the agent has one. A lease this gateway cannot read is shown as unreadable with nothing else claimed about it.

state.description: live: the agent may run. ending: an end was decided and cleanup is awaited. ended: cleanup was confirmed. interrupted: cleanup was not confirmed within its deadline, so the agent's environment is not known to be released. refused: no lease was granted and nothing ran; refusal says why. unreadable: a record of this lease is of a kind this gateway cannot read.

revision.description: Which issuance of this conversation's leases this is, counting refused ones; absent when not known.

environment.description: Where the agent runs. here: the gateway's own machine. ssh: a machine the gateway reaches over SSH, named by host, whose `nessa env serve` runs the agent's harness next to its files. peer: a paired environment, named by host, whose `nessa env serve` dials this gateway and runs the agent's harness next to its files.

host.description: The machine the agent runs on: for ssh, the OpenSSH destination as config.json names it; for peer, `peer:` and the paired environment's device key in lowercase hex. Present exactly when environment is ssh or peer.

sandbox.description: The sandbox granted, or for a refused lease the one asked for. harness_default: whatever the agent's harness encloses by default, configured by nothing Nessa sets, and nothing more. none: nothing encloses what runs beyond the account the environment runs as.

cause.description: Why the lease is ending or ended: the first cause recorded. lost: the environment no longer held it, for example because the gateway started again or the connection to it was lost. idle: the agent sat idle with nobody following the conversation, past limits.agentIdleSeconds, and the gateway stopped it; the conversation stays open and the next message starts the agent again, resuming its provider session.

cleanup.description: What the environment reported releasing, once it has: confirmed, released cooperatively; forced, released by forced termination; not_held, the environment holds nothing for the lease, though whether something started under it before the environment last started outlived it is not known. On an interrupted lease this is the evidence that arrived after its deadline.

refusal.description: Why the lease was refused. sandbox_unavailable: the sandbox asked for is not one both the agent's binding and the environment can enforce. environment_unreachable: the environment could not be reached, or did not answer in time. environment_version_mismatch: the copy of this build the environment holds, where the gateway installs it, speaks another lease protocol, so nothing was sent to it. environment_busy: the environment is serving another connection, or the organization's paired environments already run as many agent leases or commands as config.json limits.organizationLeases and limits.organizationCommands allow. agent_unavailable: the environment cannot run this conversation's agent. environment_platform_unsupported: the environment had no copy of this build, and runs on a system or processor this build has no copy for (its own executable, or the release build of it for that platform), so nothing was installed or sent. environment_install_failed: the environment had no copy of this build, and installing one failed: the release build for its platform could not be downloaded or was not the one pinned, or what arrived did not match what was sent, did not run there, or could not be stored; nothing was sent.

droppedEvents.description: Events that arrived after the lease ended and were dropped rather than applied.

commands.description: Commands the agent started under this lease that have not yet ended; absent when none. Present only on a live or ending lease.

workspace.description: Working directory on the gateway host, not the client filesystem.

ConversationRuntime.description: Runtime configuration selected by the gateway composition for this conversation.

ConversationNoticeKind.description: Which local decision a notice records. review is a declined review. hook is a permission-review hook that stopped the turn or closed the session. deadline is a deadline that settled its review. The three may share one decimal id.

offset.description: Zero-based SDK observation offset within the owning execution, used to preserve order.

kind.description: Text, exposed thought content, a tool call, or a Nessa-owned runtime notice. A tool call is one part however many updates it has, at its first update's offset; its current state is its entry in tools.

text.description: Exact text fragment for text, thought, or local notice observations; empty for a tool call.

toolId.description: The tool call's identity, which names its entry in tools; empty otherwise.

noticeId.description: Decimal identity of a local notice; empty otherwise. A review notice uses the declined-review id. A hook notice and a deadline notice use the permission id. Those identities are independent, so one decimal may name each of them; noticeKind says which decision it is.

noticeKind.description: Which local decision this notice is. Absent on every part that is not a local notice.

messageId.description: Opaque provider message identity; only fragments with the same identity may be combined.

ConversationPart.description: One ordered observation fragment in a bounded execution projection; offsets may have gaps.

ConversationPermissionAsk.description: What a review asks the person to allow: running a tool (tool) — the agent's tool call, or a tool an MCP App asked to call on its own server — or an MCP App sending one message in the conversation as them (message; mcp.sendMessage, where toolName is the app's own tool and argumentsJson is {"text": …}, the message exactly as it would be sent). The agent's reviews are always tool.

ConversationPermissionOriginKind.description: Who asked for a review: the conversation's agent (harness), or an MCP App (app), asking to call a tool of its own server or to send a message as the person (ask). The agent's approval mode never applies to an app's review.

ConversationPermissionOrigin.description: Who asked for this review. For harness, the review's executionId and toolId are the agent's tool call being reviewed. For app, they are the app's identity — the tool call whose UI it is, which has normally finished — and server and tool name the tool the app asked to call, or for a message (ask: message) the app's own server and tool (required for app, absent for harness). A harness review is shown only while its execution runs; an app review while the app waits on it, whatever its tool call's state. Answer either kind with conversation.answer or conversation.cancel.

server.description: For app: the app's server, on which the tool would be called.

tool.description: For app: the tool the app asked to call, the review's toolName.

McpAppReference.description: An MCP App, by the tool call whose UI it is, in its conversation. The gateway checks it is an MCP call of the server the request names, and that its result carried a resourceUri. It is not authenticated beyond the caller's credential: the call is recorded as the app's, on the person's behalf. instanceId names which mount of it is asking.

executionId.description: The execution the app's tool call belongs to.

instanceId.description: The host's own UUID for this mount of the app. One tool call can be mounted more than once (inline, in a pane) and again after it was torn down; reviews and tickets are kept per mount, and mcp.releaseApp releases only that one. Policy and audit name the app by executionId and toolId.

McpReleaseAppParams.description: The host tore an app's mount down (mcp.releaseApp): every review that mount has open is withdrawn and its waiting call answered mcp_cancelled, and every resource ticket issued to it is released. Releasing a mount with nothing open succeeds too. Answered with ConversationMutationResult. It travels on the control lane, never the app lane, so held calls can never stop an app being released.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

McpSendMessageParams.description: An MCP App sends a message into its conversation (mcp.sendMessage, MCP Apps ui/message): the person's turn, written by the app on their behalf and shown in the transcript as the app's (ConversationMessage.app). Every message waits for the person's approval in the conversation's permissions, origin {kind: app}, answered with conversation.answer or conversation.cancel whatever the approval mode. Refused turn_running while a turn runs or input waits, so it is never queued behind the person's own; any other refusal of the message is its own conversation code. The same requestId again, from the same mount, is the same turn: one the agent has already is not asked again, and the agent settles it, the same text answering the first delivery and other text submission_conflict; one sent again while the first is still in review or being sent is refused temporarily_unavailable. It travels on the app lane.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

server.description: The MCP server's configured name: the app's own server. Any other is refused mcp_server_mismatch.

text.description: The message, as text: at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes, what conversation.send takes (invalid_request past it, refused before anything is recorded), and not empty (invalid_request, refused before anything is recorded). Blank text, whitespace only, is invalid_request too, refused on record by the conversation. Past the conversation's own input bound, which is never larger, it is refused mcp_request_too_large. It is shown whole in its review, which must fit the 16 000 bytes an app's review may take of the view, encoded; text heavy in quotes or control characters can be past that while within 8192 bytes (mcp_request_too_large, and no review is opened).

McpSendMessageResult.description: The conversation's agent took the message.

executionId.description: The turn the message became, as the transcript names it.

McpUpdateModelContextParams.description: An MCP App gives the model context (mcp.updateModelContext, MCP Apps ui/update-model-context), in place of what this mount gave before; an update with neither text nor structuredContentJson, or with only an empty text, clears it. It is held for the mount until the next message admitted into the conversation while nothing runs and no input waits, the person's or an app's, carries it ahead of what the message says; it is not shown in the transcript. That message takes it as it is read, and it is held no longer. If the message is then refused, it is lost, recorded as dropped not_sent; if its turn fails, it is lost; either way the app may give it again. A message queued behind a running turn, or steered into one, carries none and leaves it held. A release of the mount (mcp.releaseApp) or the end of the conversation's opening drops it unsent while it is still held. A conversation's updates are taken one at a time, each recorded before it is held. Each part takes at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes (invalid_request past it, refused before anything is recorded), and text and structured content together at most 8192 (mcp_request_too_large past it); at most 4 mounts of a conversation hold a context at once (temporarily_unavailable for another). Answered with ConversationMutationResult. It travels on the app lane.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

server.description: The MCP server's configured name: the app's own server. Any other is refused mcp_server_mismatch.

text.description: The context as text: at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes (invalid_request past it). Empty is none.

structuredContentJson.description: The context's structured content: one JSON object, encoded (invalid_request if it is not one, or past 8192 UTF-8 bytes), held exactly as given. Absent is none.

McpCallToolParams.description: An MCP App calls a tool of its own server (mcp.callTool). Allowed only for a tool its conversation's own session last listed with visibility including app. A tool that is destructive — readOnlyHint is not true and destructiveHint is not false, so a tool with no annotations is — first waits for the person's approval in the conversation's permissions, whatever the approval mode; the call is answered when they answer, when the review expires (x-mcpAppCallTiming.reviewDeadlineMs), or when it is withdrawn. App calls travel on a lane of their own, 4 at once per socket, at most 3 of them from one mount, so one app's waiting reviews cannot take the lane; past either they are refused temporarily_unavailable.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

server.description: The MCP server's configured name: the app's own server. A call naming any other is refused mcp_server_mismatch.

tool.description: The tool to call on that server.

argumentsJson.description: The tool's arguments: one JSON object, encoded, at most 32 KiB (mcp_request_too_large past it, invalid_request if it is not an object), sent as parsed — re-encoded, a duplicate key's last value kept — and shown so in a destructive tool's review, which may take at most 16 000 bytes of the view (mcp_request_too_large past it). Absent is none.

resultJson.description: The MCP CallToolResult the server answered — content, structuredContent, isError, _meta — re-encoded as one JSON object, at most 56 KiB measured as the JSON string this field is (past it, the call is refused mcp_result_too_large instead). isError true is a result for the app, not a refusal.

McpReadResourceParams.description: An MCP App reads a resource of its own server (mcp.readResource). The gateway reads it once, holds those bytes, and answers what they are and a ticket that serves exactly them over HTTP (GET /mcp-resources, the ticket in the x-nessa-resource-ticket header): the bytes never travel on the socket. App calls share their own lane, as mcp.callTool's.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

server.description: The MCP server's configured name: the app's own server. A call naming any other is refused mcp_server_mismatch.

uri.description: The resource's URI on that server.

McpUiCsp.description: The CSP the app asked for (_meta.ui.csp): origins only, each list at most 64 of at most 512 bytes. No network when empty.

resourceDomains.description: Origins for scripts, styles, images, fonts and media.

McpUiPermissions.description: What the app asked of the host (_meta.ui.permissions). Each is true only when asked for as {} or true; nothing else is ever granted.

McpReadResourceResult.description: What the gateway read, and the ticket for its bytes. The host fetches GET /mcp-resources with the ticket in the x-nessa-resource-ticket header — never in a URL — checks the bytes' SHA-256 against sha256 before rendering, and treats a mismatch as a failure to load.

mimeType.description: An MCP App's HTML; any other resource is refused mcp_app_unknown.

size.description: The bytes' length: at most 4 MiB.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of exactly the bytes the ticket serves.

ticket.description: Single use, 256 random bits (base64url), valid for expiresInMs, bound to the conversation and the app. It is the whole authority to fetch the bytes, as an upload ticket is: keep it out of URLs and logs.

expiresInMs.description: How long the ticket can be redeemed.

csp.description: The CSP the app asked for.

permissions.description: What the app asked of the host.

domain.description: The dedicated origin the app asked for, when it did.

prefersBorder.description: Whether the app asked for a border, when it said.

McpRemoteErrorDetails.description: The server's own JSON-RPC error, attached to a refusal coded mcp_remote_error, or mcp_server_remote_error from mcpServers.inspect.

message.description: The server's message, at most 512 characters, control characters as spaces.

McpServerKind.description: How a configured MCP server is reached. stdio: the gateway starts it as a local process and speaks MCP over its standard input and output. remote: the gateway connects to an HTTP endpoint. A remote entry has id and url, and no command, args, or env.

McpServerListEntry.description: One server as config.json stores it now, which mcpServers.list reads: the stored file, not the live set. A hand edit to the file is listed at once and reaches the live set, and new conversations, at the next save or remove or the next start. Variable values never leave the gateway; only their names are listed. A stdio entry includes command, args and envNames. A remote entry includes id and url, and none of those three.

name.description: The server's name, unique among the configured servers.

command.description: The absolute path of the executable the gateway starts.

args.description: The arguments it is started with, in order.

envNames.description: The names of the variables it is given over the gateway's own, sorted by name. Never their values.

enabled.description: Whether it is stored turned on. A server saved on is given to new conversations from that save; one turned on by hand in the file, from the next save or remove or the next start. A server turned off stays stored, and can be inspected.

managed.description: Nessa's own server: listed, never saved or removed through these methods.

id.description: The remote server's durable id. Present exactly when kind is remote. A rename does not change it. A save cannot choose it.

url.description: The remote endpoint. Present exactly when kind is remote.

authorization.description: Redacted authorization facts for a remote server. Absent for stdio, and for a remote with no record yet. Never a token.

McpAuthorizationPhase.description: Where a remote server's authorization stands. unauthenticated: the endpoint accepted a probe with no credentials. consent_needed: a person must authorize, or discovery has not finished. pending_consent: a consent URL is outstanding. ready: a usable token is stored. scope_required: the last call was refused for scope and was not retried. authorization_incomplete: an exchange or refresh was not settled. revoking: revoke is in progress. revocation_incomplete: local cleanup or its evidence did not finish.

McpRemoteObservation.description: What the authorization server did with a revocation. acknowledged: its revocation endpoint answered success. unsupported: it advertised no revocation endpoint. unconfirmed: the call was sent and the answer was not retained, or it failed.

McpServerAuthorization.description: Redacted authorization facts mcpServers.list may attach to a remote server. No token, refresh secret, or authorization code is included.

generation.description: The token generation. A refresh that published a replacement increments it.

tokenExpired.description: Whether the stored access token is past its expiry or was marked unavailable.

refreshFailing.description: Whether a refresh is in flight, or the last refresh was not settled.

scopeRequired.description: Whether the last call was refused for scope. The call was not retried.

remoteObservation.description: The last revocation's remote observation, when a revoke has been asked.

domainsDigest.description: The domain-set digest a person acknowledged for this server, when one has been.

McpServersAuthorizeParams.description: Wire input for mcpServers.authorize: begin consent for the remote server id at the listed revision. A stdio server cannot be authorized. Status and list reads do not open a browser; this method returns a consent URL when one is required.

revision.description: The revision the caller last listed.

McpServersAuthorizeResult.description: Result of mcpServers.authorize. No token is included. pending_consent carries the URL the host opens and the deadline of that attempt. ready means a token is already usable. not_required means the endpoint accepted a probe with no credentials.

attemptId.description: The consent attempt, present for pending_consent.

consentUrl.description: The authorization URL, present for pending_consent. It carries no code verifier.

deadlineMs.description: When the consent attempt expires, as milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Present for pending_consent.

generation.description: The token generation, present for ready.

McpServersRevokeParams.description: Wire input for mcpServers.revoke: fence the remote server id at the listed revision. Local sessions of that server are closed. The result keeps drain, secret deletion, remote observation and evidence apart; an incomplete revoke is not reported as settled.

revision.description: The revision the caller last listed.

McpServersRevokeResult.description: Result of mcpServers.revoke. settled is true only after the local drain, secret deletion, remote observation and required evidence all finished. An incomplete result stays incomplete.

localDrained.description: Whether local sessions of this server were closed.

secretDeleted.description: Whether the private token is gone.

remoteObservation.description: What the authorization server did, when that was observed.

evidenceAcknowledged.description: Whether the outcome record was acknowledged.

McpServersAuthorizationHeldDetails.description: Attached to a refusal coded mcp_servers_authorization_held. The configuration file was written. The live set was not replaced, because the previous token binding could not be fenced.

applied.description: Whether the configuration file was written. True: it was, and the live set still has the previous URL.

McpServersListResult.description: Result of mcpServers.list: the stored servers and the revision a save or remove must name.

revision.description: A digest of the stored server list, keyed with a secret this gateway process mints at start: compare for equality only, and list again after a restart, since the same list has another revision then. A save or remove naming any other revision is refused mcp_servers_revision_conflict.

servers.description: The stored servers in stored order, then the managed one.

McpServerEnvEntry.description: One variable a saved server is given.

name.description: The variable's name: ASCII letters, digits and _, 1 to x-mcpServerRules.environmentNameMaxBytes bytes, not starting with a digit. NESSA_MCP_SESSION is reserved.

value.description: Its value, or null to keep the value stored for this name on the server being saved, only when the save launches that server as stored apart from the kept values: the same command and args, and the same variable names, each other one null or given its stored value. A save that changes anything else (the command, an argument, a variable added, left out or given another value) must give every value again. Required: an entry without value is refused invalid_request, so leaving it out never keeps a value by accident. A null for a name with no stored value is refused mcp_servers_invalid (environment_value_missing).

McpServerInput.description: A server as mcpServers.save stores it. kind stdio requires command, args and env, and refuses url. kind remote requires url, and refuses command, args and env. A remote save cannot choose the stored id.

name.description: Its name: ASCII letters, digits, - and _, 1 to x-mcpServerRules.nameMaxBytes bytes, without __ and not starting or ending with _. nessa is reserved.

command.description: The absolute path of its executable.

args.description: Its arguments, in order: at most x-mcpServerRules.maxArgs, each at most x-mcpServerRules.argMaxBytes bytes. Never put credentials here; use env.

env.description: Every variable it is given over the gateway's own, each name once; they are stored, and listed, sorted by name whatever order they are given in. A stored variable left out is removed.

enabled.description: Whether new conversations are given it.

url.description: The remote endpoint. Required when kind is remote, and refused when kind is stdio. The gateway checks it; this field does not restate that rule.

McpServersSaveParams.description: Wire input for mcpServers.save: store a server, adding it or replacing the one under its name, or renaming the one under previousName, in one write.

revision.description: The revision the caller last listed.

previousName.description: The name the server is stored under now, when it is being renamed. Unknown: mcp_servers_not_found.

server.description: The server as it should be stored.

McpServersRemoveParams.description: Wire input for mcpServers.remove: take a stored server out of the configuration.

revision.description: The revision the caller last listed.

name.description: The stored server's name. Unknown: mcp_servers_not_found.

McpServersWriteResult.description: Result of mcpServers.save and mcpServers.remove: the published configuration's revision. New conversations get the new server set; running ones keep theirs.

revision.description: The stored server list's revision now, for this gateway process.

live.description: Whether new conversations get the stored list as now written. False when the gateway is stopping (the next start reads the file), or when a remove left a list edited by hand still past a bound (more servers than x-mcpServerRules.maxServers, or one that breaks a rule): the removed server is out of the live set all the same, and the rest stay as they were until a change brings the list within its bounds.

McpServerProblemCode.description: Why a saved server, or a stored one inspected, is invalid. The numbers are x-mcpServerRules, which the gateway's own rules publish. too_many: more than maxServers servers, the managed one included. duplicate_name: another server has the name. name: not 1 to nameMaxBytes bytes of ASCII letters, digits, - and _, holds __, or starts or ends with _. command: not an absolute UTF-8 path. arguments: more than maxArgs, or one over argMaxBytes bytes or holding NUL. environment_name: a variable name that is not ASCII letters, digits and _ (1 to environmentNameMaxBytes bytes, not starting with a digit). reserved_environment_name: NESSA_MCP_SESSION. environment_value: a value holding NUL. environment_value_missing: a null value for a name with no stored value, or in a save that changes anything else the server is launched with. environment_name_repeated: a variable given twice, which is said before a value missing. url: a remote endpoint that is not https, and not http on an explicit loopback host, or that carries userinfo or a fragment. duplicate_server_id: two remote servers are stored with one id.

McpServersInvalidDetails.description: Attached to a refusal coded mcp_servers_invalid.

server.description: The server the problem is about, as it is stored or was asked to be saved: present for every problem but too_many, so an entry added to config.json by hand is named.

name.description: The variable the problem is about, for environment_name, reserved_environment_name, environment_value, environment_value_missing and environment_name_repeated; for environment_name, any byte of it that is not UTF-8 replaced. Never a value.

McpServersRevisionConflictDetails.description: Attached to a refusal coded mcp_servers_revision_conflict.

revision.description: The stored revision now; list again before retrying.

McpServersAuditUnavailableDetails.description: Attached to a refusal coded audit_unavailable from an mcpServers method. Nothing is rolled back; mcpServers.list shows where things stand.

applied.description: For mcpServers.save and mcpServers.remove: whether the change was published all the same; the live set may not have been replaced if the gateway is stopping. For mcpServers.inspect: whether the server was started — or its launch had begun, when the work failed unexpectedly after that.

code.description: What the request would have been answered had its record been written: the refusal or failure that stopped it, or mcp_servers_storage_unavailable for a change published but not made durable. Absent when nothing stopped it, or when the first record could not be written and nothing was done. Never audit_unavailable.

McpServersConfigTooLargeDetails.description: Attached to a refusal coded mcp_servers_config_too_large that answers mcpServers.list: the stored list would not fit one frame (an entry added to config.json by hand). mcpServers.remove by name, naming this revision, still works, and is how the list is made to fit again.

revision.description: The stored revision, as mcpServers.list would have answered it.

McpServersStorageUnavailableDetails.description: Attached to a refusal coded mcp_servers_storage_unavailable. mcpServers.list shows where things stand.

applied.description: true: the change was published — config.json replaced, and the live set followed as far as it could (replaced, withdrawn, or kept during shutdown or when the list is past a bound); list again to see the current state — but its directory could not be synced, so a crash could still lose it; its outcome record says durable false. false: nothing was written, applied or started.

McpServersInspectParams.description: Wire input for mcpServers.inspect: start the stored server under name once, outside any conversation, list what it offers, then stop it. A server turned off can be inspected; a server not yet saved cannot. At most x-mcpServerInspect.maxConcurrent run at once, each within x-mcpServerInspect.deadlineMs.

name.description: The stored server's name. Unknown: mcp_servers_not_found; nessa: mcp_servers_reserved_name.

McpServersInspectCut.description: Which bound left an inspection incomplete. tools: the server listed more than x-mcpServerInspect.maxToolPages pages, or more tools than the gateway reads from one server; the rest are not listed. ui: more distinct UI resources than x-mcpServerInspect.maxUiReads; tools past it are listed without ui. bytes: the answer would pass 64 KiB; tools were dropped from the end until it fits. stopping: the gateway began to stop after the server was started; the reading was dropped and the server's process group killed, and tools is empty.

McpInspectedUi.description: A tool's MCP App as the server declares it: the resource, and the CSP and permissions it asks for, read as mcp.readResource reads them.

uri.description: The ui:// resource the tool declares.

csp.description: The CSP the app asks for.

permissions.description: What the app asks of the host.

McpInspectedTool.description: One tool a server lists, as mcpServers.inspect reports it.

name.description: The tool's name on the server.

readOnlyHint.description: annotations.readOnlyHint, when the server gives it as a boolean.

destructiveHint.description: annotations.destructiveHint, when the server gives it as a boolean.

ui.description: Its MCP App, when it declares one and it was read.

McpServersInspectResult.description: Result of mcpServers.inspect: the tools the server listed, with each MCP App's CSP and permissions. The server has been stopped and its process group killed before this is answered.

complete.description: Whether every tool and UI the server offered is here.

cut.description: Which bound left it incomplete; present exactly when complete is false.

tools.description: The tools, in the server's order.

McpServersErrorCode.description: Why the gateway refused an mcpServers method it dispatched. mcp_servers_not_configured: this gateway holds no live MCP server set to manage (not Unix, no agents configured, or MCP off this run because its relay socket could not be bound, a path was not UTF-8, or no key for its configuration digests could be drawn). mcp_servers_invalid: the saved server or the resulting set breaks a rule; or, for mcpServers.inspect, the stored server does (an entry added to config.json by hand), and it was not started (details: McpServersInvalidDetails). mcp_servers_reserved_name: the request names nessa, Nessa's own server. mcp_servers_not_found: no server is stored under the name. mcp_servers_revision_conflict: the stored list changed since the caller's revision (details: McpServersRevisionConflictDetails). mcp_servers_busy: another change held config.json's lock too long, and nothing was written; or, for mcpServers.inspect, x-mcpServerInspect.maxConcurrent inspections are running already, and nothing was started. mcp_servers_config_invalid: config.json does not parse, as it is or as it would be written (a stored server name past x-mcpServerRules.nameMaxBytes among it, so every request naming a stored server fits one frame). It is never repaired. mcp_servers_config_too_large: the result would pass 64 KiB as written, which is pretty-printed or, when only that fits, compact; or, for mcpServers.save, the resulting mcpServers.list answer would not fit one frame for the longest request id, and nothing was written (a remove is never refused for that); or, for mcpServers.list, the stored list would not fit one frame (details: McpServersConfigTooLargeDetails), or config.json itself passes 64 KiB (no details). mcp_servers_storage_unavailable (details: McpServersStorageUnavailableDetails): config.json could not be read, locked or published, or the work failed unexpectedly before it published or before the inspected server's launch began — its outcome recorded failed, panicked — and the stored file and the live set are unchanged (applied false); or the change was published, and the live set followed as far as it could (replaced, withdrawn, or kept during shutdown or when the list is past a bound), but config.json's directory could not be synced, so the change may not survive a crash (applied true); list again to see the current state. mcp_servers_stopping: the gateway is stopping, and nothing was started or written: the request came after shutdown began, and nothing was recorded; or, for mcpServers.inspect, shutdown began before the server was started, or the MCP client refused to start it, as the inspection's outcome record says (stopping, started false). Changes admitted before shutdown finish, and are recorded, before the gateway stops its MCP servers; an inspection already started is cut instead (McpServersInspectCut stopping). audit_unavailable: a record of the change or inspection could not be made durable, or the work failed unexpectedly after the change was published or the server's launch began, so no outcome was recorded (details: McpServersAuditUnavailableDetails). The mcp_server_ codes answer mcpServers.inspect, whose server was stopped on each: mcp_server_start_failed, its process could not be launched (a missing command among them); mcp_server_timed_out, it did not finish within x-mcpServerInspect.deadlineMs, or did not answer a request in time; mcp_server_gone, it ended before it answered; mcp_server_malformed, it answered something that is not MCP, or a UI resource that is not an MCP App within its bounds; mcp_server_remote_error, it answered a request with a JSON-RPC error (details: McpRemoteErrorDetails). mcp_server_unreachable, a remote endpoint could not be reached and nothing was retained. mcp_server_unauthorized, the endpoint refused the caller; the answer carries no token. mcp_server_insufficient_scope, the caller's scope was not enough and the call was not retried. mcp_server_session_collision, another opening already holds that upstream session id, and this inspection did not delete it. mcp_servers_authorization_held (details: McpServersAuthorizationHeldDetails): a save or remove wrote config.json, and the live set was not replaced because the previous remote token could not be fenced; applied is true. mcp_servers_store_unavailable: this platform has no private token writer, so authorize did not start. mcp_servers_registration_unsupported: the authorization server does not offer dynamic client registration. mcp_servers_discovery_failed: discovery, the callback, or the token exchange was refused, and no token was stored. mcp_servers_authorization_incomplete: an exchange or refresh was sent and its result was not retained, so the token is fenced until authorize is repeated.

ConversationErrorCode.description: Typed rejection code carried by a conversation command the gateway dispatched and refused. Branch on these instead of message text. These are not every code a conversation request can receive: access and routing failures are answered by the session before a conversation command is dispatched, and carry their own codes. agent_startup_deadline means the agent was still starting when its budget expired, so nothing reached the provider and the same command is safe to repeat; it normally succeeds once the runtime is warm, but a launch whose process could not be confirmed stopped keeps that conversation blocked. invalid_request and agent_not_configured reject the command until their cause is addressed. agent_not_configured, agent_unsupported and conversations_not_configured are three different situations and only one of them is fixed by configuring an agent: the gateway runs no conversations at all, it names no runtime under the agent this conversation asked for, or no build here can open that conversation's agent. sandbox_unavailable means no lease could be granted to run the agent because the sandbox it asks for is not one both its agent binding and the place it would run can enforce; nothing ran, the refusal is in the conversation's records, and repeating the command fails the same way until that configuration changes. environment_not_configured is a create naming an SSH destination config.json does not name, or a conversation created on one it no longer names; nothing ran. environment_unavailable is an SSH environment that could not be reached, is serving another connection, or cannot run this conversation's agent: no lease was granted, the refusal is in the conversation's records, and the same command may succeed once the environment is reachable. environment_version_mismatch is an SSH environment whose copy of this build, where the gateway installs it, says it speaks another lease protocol: nothing was sent to it. environment_platform_unsupported is an SSH environment with no copy of this build that runs on a system or processor this build has no copy for: the gateway installs its own executable, or on another platform the release build of it pinned for that platform, which a development build has none of; nothing was installed or sent. Run the conversation on a host like the gateway's, or from a release. environment_install_failed is an SSH environment with no copy of this build where installing one failed: the release build for its platform could not be downloaded or was not the one pinned, or what arrived did not match what was sent, did not run there, or could not be stored, and nothing was sent; the gateway's environment audit says which, and the same command tries the install again. linked_file_unreachable is a message linking a file by its path on this machine, sent to a conversation that runs on an SSH host: the host cannot read this machine's files and would read whatever it has at that path, so nothing was recorded or sent; send the message without it, or attach an image, whose bytes travel with it. The image codes answer `attachment.begin`, a message naming uploads, and `artifact.read`: image_input_unsupported is a model that takes no images, so no ticket and no message with one will ever be taken; attachment_not_found is an image or artifact this conversation does not hold — never uploaded or published into it, expired, or released when it closed — which also ends an artifact.read; attachment_unavailable is one it holds but could not read; attachment_capacity is no room for another upload right now; attachment_storage_unavailable is the gateway unable to keep the bytes. attachment_cleanup_unavailable is a close that did happen, whose release of this conversation's uploads did not, and is the one image code that is not a refusal of the command. conversation_deleted refuses every command its owner sends on a conversation somebody deleted, except deleting it again; anyone else is told conversation_not_found. Its identity is never reused, so a surface still holding it should let it go. conversation_erasure_incomplete is a delete that did happen — the conversation is gone and every command on it is refused — whose erasure of stored data did not finish; repeating the delete, and each gateway start, tries again, but an agent that keeps refusing to delete its own session, or a damaged history, needs the operator. The mcp_ codes refuse an MCP App's request (mcp.callTool, mcp.readResource, mcp.sendMessage, mcp.updateModelContext): mcp_app_unknown, the app is not an MCP tool call with a UI in this conversation, or the resource is not an app's; mcp_server_mismatch, it names another server than the app's; mcp_tool_not_for_app, the tool is not listed with visibility including app; mcp_session_unavailable, the conversation has no open session of that server, or it ended; mcp_approval_denied and mcp_approval_expired, the person refused, or did not answer within x-mcpAppCallTiming.reviewDeadlineMs; mcp_cancelled, the review was withdrawn because the request was cancelled, the app was torn down, or the conversation ended, or, with no review withdrawn, the app's mount was released or the opening it was drawn in ended (closed, deleted, stopped, another begun, or the gateway stopping) before the request took effect, which for mcp.sendMessage sends nothing and opens nothing; mcp_request_too_large and mcp_result_too_large, past a request's bound (the arguments' 32 KiB, a message's input bound or its review's room, a context's 8 KiB) and a result's 56 KiB; turn_running also refuses an app's message while a turn runs or input waits; mcp_timed_out, the server did not answer in time; mcp_remote_error, the server answered with a JSON-RPC error (McpRemoteErrorDetails), or with something that is no MCP answer (no details). mcp_unauthorized, the remote endpoint refused the caller and the tool was not run; the answer carries no token. mcp_unreachable, the remote endpoint could not be reached and nothing was retained. mcp_insufficient_scope, the caller's scope was not enough and the call was not retried. These three are not mcp_session_unavailable: the session was not reported as ended. capabilities_refused: conversation.share asked Cedar's grant.comment or grant.drive before writing those capabilities and was denied. details.policies names the Cedar policy ids; it is empty when no permit matched. Nothing was written. The share does not match a gateway principal on its own. share_target_not_paired: conversation.share named a credential that is not an active paired device or peer gateway of the conversation's owner holding conversation.read. share_grant_changed: conversation.share or conversation.unshare named an expectedPolicyRevision the device's grant no longer holds: it was changed or revoked since that revision was read; nothing was changed, and conversation.shares says what it holds now. idempotency_conflict: conversation.message reused a requestId that already left another note (another text, delivery, surface or authority; the same grant at a later policy revision is the same authority); nothing was saved, and the first note stands. message_quota_exceeded: conversation.message found the conversation holding its most notes, or its author past its rate; nothing was saved. drive_policy_unenforceable: a Drive grant's conversation.send or conversation.steer where its tools cannot all be checked against the grant's tool policy (an OpenCode conversation, an approval mode other than ask, native hooks allowed, or the policy unreadable); nothing was saved or sent, and the same command fails the same way until the owner changes that. revoked: a Drive grant's conversation.send, or a steer that is queued rather than injected, whose grant was revoked or changed after the admitted revision was read and before the turn was saved; nothing was saved, the command receipt is settled as no_effect, and retrying that same request is answered revoked again. A new request is admitted only under the grant as it stands now. revoked_after_save: a native steer that was saved and then refused because the grant moved before injection; the saved attempt is settled as refused and nothing reached the agent. The command receipt is settled as refused_after_save, and retrying that same request is answered revoked_after_save again and is not admitted again. Retrying it as a different initiation is a submission conflict. unavailable_after_save: a native steer that was saved and then could not be checked because the grant record could not be read before injection; nothing reached the agent. The command receipt is settled as unavailable_after_save, and retrying that same request is answered unavailable_after_save again and is not admitted again. A new request is admitted only under the grant as it stands now. channel_not_found: conversation.create named a channelId the caller has no channel under; nothing was created.

Looked up at each dial. It carries no trust: the peer must still present its pinned key through it. Null clears it, so the peer is read only at its address.

PeerRelayParams.description: Wire input for peer.relay: set or clear the relay kept for a peer. A read of that peer in progress is stopped first, and the next read uses the new relay.

PeerPhase.description: Where this gateway's enrollment with a peer stands, as this gateway last heard. pending: claimed, waiting on the peer's owner to approve, or not yet confirmed. active: the peer issued this gateway a credential. revoked: the peer ended the enrollment (its owner revoked the credential, or denied, cancelled or let expire the claim), its retained cache is removed and it is no longer read; only peer.forget helps. unreadable: the peer's record is there but this build cannot read it, or it was made with a key that is no longer this gateway's; only peer.forget helps.

peerKey.description: The peer's key: what identifies the peer, whatever address it answers at. Its TLS key is pinned to exactly this.

address.description: The address that last answered as this peer. Absent when the record is unreadable.

relay.description: The relay this gateway asks for the peer at when its address does not answer. Absent when none is set, or the record is unreadable.

credentialId.description: The credential the peer issued this gateway, once active. An identifier, not a secret.

receiverId.description: The receiver the peer paired with that credential, once active.

sync.description: What this gateway's poller last saw reading the peer. Only in peer.list, and only for a pending or active peer; absent for a revoked or unreadable one, and in the results of peer.enroll and peer.forget.

PeerGateway.description: One peer gateway this gateway enrolled into. Result of peer.enroll, peer.relay and peer.forget; peer.list adds sync for a pending or active peer.

PeerSyncState.description: How reading a peer last went, since this gateway started. waiting: not read yet, or still pending on the peer. synced: the last read brought the retained cache up to what the peer grants. syncing: the last read saved some of what the peer grants and stopped at a bound (a page bound or its time budget); the next continues it. A read an owner command stops leaves the state as it was. unreachable: the peer could not be reached, or the last read ran out of its time budget before it saved anything; reads back off. away: the peer's address did not answer and its relay said the peer is not registered with it (asleep, quit or offline, as far as the relay can tell; nothing authenticates that word); the retained cache is kept and readable, and reads back off as for unreachable. failed: the peer answered but the read failed; reads back off. quota: this gateway's retained cache of the peer is full; each read still withdraws what the peer no longer grants, and reads back off until the peer grants less.

lastSyncedAtMs.description: When the last read of this peer that saved something, or found the cache up to date, finished, in Unix milliseconds. A failed read leaves it as it was. Absent until one has since this gateway started.

conversations.description: Conversations the peer granted that this gateway's retained cache holds, as the last read counted. Absent until one has.

PeerSync.description: What this gateway last saw reading a peer: its poller reads each pending or active peer's status and grants on a cadence.

items.description: Every peer this gateway keeps, by key.

PeerErrorCode.description: Why the gateway refused a peer method it dispatched. peer_not_configured: native pairing is off in this gateway's configuration, so it has no key to enroll with. peer_not_found: no peer with that key. peer_exists: a record for that peer is already kept; forget it first. peer_capacity: this gateway keeps as many peers as it may. peer_busy: another enrollment or forget is running; retry once it ends. A read of a peer makes a command busy only if a stopped read does not give back its turn within peer.preempt: the command stops the read and takes its turn once the read gives it back, and the read carries on later. peer_unreachable: nothing answered at the address, the connection failed, or what answered is not a gateway enrolling peers; an open port is not told from a closed one. peer_invitation_refused: the peer refused the code: no open invitation, or an expired, used or wrong code; it does not say which. peer_wrong_invitation: the code is for a device, not a gateway. peer_own_gateway: the address is this gateway's own. peer_unavailable: storage, the key or a worker failed, or the gateway is stopping and refused the command before any effect; retry later. peer_audit_unavailable: the command's audit record could not be kept; if that was before its effect nothing changed, and if after, the effect stands and peer.list shows it.

ConversationSubscriptionId.description: Opaque identity of one subscription on this connection. It grants nothing and is discarded with the connection.

incarnation.description: The stored history's incarnation. A different one means the history was replaced, and the frame is a replacement for everything held.

position.description: Decimal committed position the view was folded through, within this incarnation.

ConversationViewCursor.description: Where in the committed history a view was read. Compare positions only within one incarnation.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

after.description: The cursor of the last view this client applied. No frame behind it in the same incarnation is sent; at least one frame at or past it is.

ConversationSubscribeParams.description: Follow one conversation's view: the reply comes after the first read, then a conversation.view frame whenever what the view shows changes, until conversation.subscriptionEnded or conversation.unsubscribe.

archived.description: Follow only archived conversations when true; only unarchived ones when false or absent.

ConversationSubscribeListParams.description: Follow the caller's conversation list: the reply comes after the first list, then a conversation.listed frame whenever the list changes.

ConversationSubscribeResult.description: The subscription is live. Its first frame follows this reply.

ConversationUnsubscribeParams.description: Stop one subscription of this connection: conversation.unsubscribe stops one made by conversation.subscribe or conversation.subscribeList, agents.unsubscribe one made by agents.subscribe, and either answers unknown_subscription for the other's. A frame already being written may arrive before the reply; none arrives after it.

view.description: The same bounded replacement conversation.read returns.

ConversationViewed.description: The conversation's current view, read after a committed or live change. Replace what was held with it.

list.description: The same list conversation.list returns, cut newest first and marked incomplete when it would not fit one frame.

ConversationListed.description: The caller's current conversation list, read after a change. Replace what was held with it.

ConversationSubscriptionEndReason.description: Why a subscription ended. lagging: a frame waited longer than x-subscriptionLimits.deliveryTimeoutMs to be written; subscribe again from lastDelivered. refused: a read or its access check was refused, with code. source_closed: the change source closed; subscribe again. too_large: a frame would not fit the frame bound.

code.description: For refused: the conversation error code, or unauthorized or forbidden when access was refused.

lastEventCursor.description: Last semantic event cursor written, or the supplied after cursor if no batch was written. A written cursor records socket delivery, not application processing. Resume from your application's own last-applied batch cursor.

lastDelivered.description: Where a view subscription resumes from: the cursor of the last view frame written or, when none was, the after it was opened with. Absent for a list, and for a view subscription opened without after that wrote no frame.

ConversationSubscriptionEnded.description: The subscription's one terminal frame. Nothing of it follows.

ConversationSubscriptionErrorCode.description: Refusals of subscribe and unsubscribe beside the conversation error codes a refused first read carries. subscription_capacity: the connection's published limit is full. subscription_duplicate: this connection already follows that target; the agent catalog is one target, so a connection follows it at most once. unknown_subscription: no such live subscription on this connection, or one the other unsubscribe stops. cursor_ahead: after names a position past the stored history.

ConversationMessageDelivery.description: What becomes of a note once it is saved. record_only saves it with its author and never hands it to the model by itself. next_turn saves it pending and hands it to the model, labelled with its author, with the next turn a person starts with conversation.send while the agent is idle: never with a steer, a turn queued behind another, or an app's message. That turn takes at most 8 notes, the oldest first, and only those whose author still holds the right to leave them, checked as the turn is admitted; a note whose author's grant was revoked or lowered below comment is retired permission_lost instead, and one still pending 24 hours after it was accepted is retired expired.

ConversationMessageState.description: Where a saved note stands. recorded is a record_only note: saved, with nothing waiting to deliver it, and it stays recorded. pending is a next_turn note waiting for a turn to take it. assigned is a next_turn note a turn took, named by executionId; it is never pending again, whatever becomes of that turn. retired is a next_turn note no turn will take, for retiredReason.

ConversationMessageRetiredReason.description: Why a next_turn note was retired. expired: it was still pending 24 hours after it was accepted. permission_lost: when a turn was admitted, its author's grant had been revoked or lowered below comment.

ConversationUnreadable.description: One saved record this read could not apply. The transcript draws one line for it, after the turn named by afterExecutionId, and that line is where a future report action attaches.

id.description: The record's physical position, as a decimal with no leading zero.

afterExecutionId.description: The last turn accepted when the record was skipped, so the line is shown after that turn; absent when none had been.

ConversationNote.description: One note left in the conversation, as everyone who reads it sees it. A note is not a turn and not the person's message: show it apart from the turns, with its author.

messageId.description: The conversation's own name for the note, as its receipt gave it.

text.description: What the note says, exactly as it was left.

acceptedAtMs.description: When the note was accepted, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, on the gateway's clock.

executionId.description: The turn that took it; present exactly when deliveryState is assigned.

retiredReason.description: Why it was retired; present exactly when deliveryState is retired.

afterExecutionId.description: The last turn the conversation had accepted when the note was, so it is shown after that turn; absent when it was left before any turn.

ConversationNoteAuthorKind.description: owner: the conversation's owner left it. grant: someone the conversation is shared with left it, under their grant.

ConversationNoteAuthor.description: Under which authority a note was left, and from which surface: the label it carries in the transcript and to the model.

surface.description: The verified surface it was left from.

ConversationHandoff.description: A point after which the conversation's agent ran in a new session that had not seen the turns before it: a switch to another agent or model (conversation.switchAgent), or the fork the conversation began as (conversation.fork). The first turn after it was given those turns as text. Show it as a line in the transcript, after the turn it follows.

handoffId.description: The conversation's own name for the handoff.

kind.description: A switch to another agent or model, or the fork the conversation began as.

atMs.description: When it was recorded, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, on the gateway's clock.

afterExecutionId.description: The last turn the conversation held when it was recorded, which it is shown after; absent before any turn, as a fork always is.

from.description: A switch's agent and model before it; present exactly for a switch.

to.description: A switch's agent and model after it; present exactly for a switch.

turns.description: A fork's copied turns, oldest first, shown before everything the conversation said itself. Absent for a switch, and when the view left them all out.

omittedTurns.description: Copied turns left out, by the copy's own bounds or by this view's; absent when none were.

ConversationHandoffAgent.description: An agent and model a switch left or went to.

agent.description: The agent, as agents.list names it; absent when the history's provider is one this gateway has no agent for.

model.description: The model, as the agent's catalog names it.

ConversationCarriedTurn.description: One turn a fork copied, as the new conversation's agent was given it: what was said, and the agent's final reply. Text only.

said.description: What was said in the turn, when it said anything in text.

reply.description: The agent's final reply, when it gave one.

ConversationMessageParams.description: Leave a note in one conversation (conversation.message). A note is saved with its author, the caller's principal and surface and the authority it was admitted under, and starts or steers no turn: a next_turn note waits for the next turn a person starts (see ConversationMessageDelivery). The conversation's owner leaves one from its own surfaces; a paired device needs a comment or drive grant on that conversation, and is refused forbidden under a read grant and conversation_not_found where it holds none. The same requestId with the same text and delivery, from the same surface under the same authority, answers the first receipt unchanged, however long after; any other note under that requestId is refused idempotency_conflict. A conversation keeps at most 1024 notes, and one author (a principal under one authority) leaves at most 20 in any 60 seconds; past either it is refused message_quota_exceeded and nothing is saved. At most 64 next_turn notes wait for a turn at once, not counting one past its 24 hours, which the next turn retires; past that a next_turn note is refused message_quota_exceeded too. A deleted conversation refuses it conversation_deleted.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

text.description: What the note says: 1 to 8192 bytes, not all blank, kept exactly as given.

delivery.description: What becomes of the note once it is saved.

ConversationMessageReceipt.description: The receipt of a saved note. A retry of the same request answers the same note, where it stands then.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

messageId.description: The conversation's own name for the note, made when it was accepted.

acceptedAtMs.description: When the note was accepted, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, on the gateway's clock.

executionId.description: The turn that took the note; present exactly when deliveryState is assigned.

retiredReason.description: Why the note was retired; present exactly when deliveryState is retired.

ConversationMessageStatusParams.description: Read where the caller's own note stands (conversation.messageStatus), by the requestId it was left under. This writes nothing. It is admitted as conversation.message is, so a paired device needs a comment or drive grant; it finds notes by principal and requestId, so a device signed in as its owner finds the owner's notes and those of the owner's other devices, and never another principal's.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

ConversationMessageStatusResult.description: Whether the caller left a saved note under that request, and where it stands. found is false when it left no note that is saved yet. After a conversation.message that failed, a note can still be saved by a later write, so false does not make a new note safe: send the same requestId again, which saves it at most once.

found.description: True when a saved note answers this request.

requestId.description: The request that was looked up.

executionId.description: The turn that took the note; present exactly when deliveryState is assigned.

retiredReason.description: Why the note was retired; present exactly when deliveryState is retired.

PermissionRuleEffect.description: Whether a remembered rule allows or denies the tool.

PermissionRule.description: One remembered rule: a tool in one workspace, granted by the owner.

id.description: Stable rule id. A replacement keeps it.

revision.description: Revision of this rule. The audit records the one that answered.

workspace.description: Workspace path the rule is scoped to.

ConversationPermissionRulesParams.description: List the owner's remembered permission rules.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

ConversationPermissionRulesResult.description: The valid remembered rules, in the order they were stored.

requestId.description: Original action identifier.
Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

ConversationRevokePermissionRuleResult.description: Whether a rule with that id was deleted.

requestId.description: Original action identifier.

applied.description: True when a rule was deleted. False when none had this id.

PermissionReviewNotice.description: One review waiting on a person.

conversationId.description: Conversation the review belongs to.

executionId.description: Execution that owns the review.

title.description: The conversation's name as conversation.list shows it, read when this set was published, so a notice can name a conversation the client has not listed yet. Omitted when none is on record.

PermissionReviewWaiting.description: The reviews still waiting. A later event replaces this one; an empty list means none are waiting.

reviews.description: Waiting reviews, oldest first, at most 128.

ConversationEventKind.description: Committed semantic facts. A scheduling start is distinct from queued input; tool state is provider observation, not proof of physical effects; turn end is local settlement.

ConversationEventCursor.description: Opaque SDK cursor bound to one conversation and stream incarnation. Save only after applying the batch. Reuse unchanged to resume; socket sequence numbers are not cursors.

id.description: Stable semantic event identity, identical on replay.

cursor.description: Opaque checkpoint after applying this event or batch.

executionId.description: Execution this fact belongs to, when any.

toolId.description: Provider tool identity within its execution, when any.

name.description: Tool name when observed, bounded metadata only.

outcome.description: Local settlement outcome; this is not a provider acknowledgement.

ConversationEvent.description: Metadata projected from one complete committed semantic fact. No prompt, thinking, tool arguments or results are included.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

after.description: Resume strictly after the last applied semantic cursor.

replay.description: Start at the beginning when true. Omitted starts at the captured committed head. Mutually exclusive with after.

kinds.description: Event kinds to deliver; omitted delivers all supported kinds. Filtered batches still advance their cursor.

ConversationSubscribeEventsParams.description: Follow committed semantic events without opening an Agent. Replay uses complete saved facts and explicit gap refusals; default is future events. Stop with conversation.unsubscribe.

subscriptionId.description: The connection-local subscription this batch belongs to.

cursor.description: Opaque checkpoint after applying this event or batch.

events.description: Committed semantic events in source order; empty advances filtered progress.

ConversationEvents.description: An ordered bounded semantic event batch. An empty batch advances the checkpoint past filtered facts. Application checkpoints belong to the consumer.

ConversationSetModelParams.description: Change the model within the existing provider session, including while a turn runs. Effect timing follows the provider.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

model.description: Exact model identifier within the conversation provider.

ConversationSwitchAgentParams.description: Carry the conversation on under another agent, in a new session of it that is given the conversation's earlier turns as text with its next message; the transcript shows a handoff line where it happened. Refused busy while a turn runs or waits; refused invalid_request for the agent the conversation already runs on (use conversation.setModel). applied is false when the switch was not made, and the conversation stays on its agent.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID identifying the conversation within the authenticated organization.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

agent.description: The agent to carry on under, as agents.list names it.

model.description: Exact model identifier within that agent's catalog.

ConversationForkParams.description: Start a new conversation from a copy of another's turns, on the same agent, model, approval preset and environment. The new conversation's agent is given the copied turns as text with its first message, and its transcript shows them first. Idempotent for a retry of one request; the conversation identity is the caller's, as for conversation.create.

conversationId.description: The new conversation, a fresh canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

sourceConversationId.description: The conversation to copy, which must be the caller's own.

ConversationSetModelResult.description: Durably confirmed model and approval preset, with native effect timing.

requestId.description: Original action identifier.

model.description: Exact model identifier within the conversation provider.

approvalMode.description: Approval preset acknowledged with the model selection.

effect.description: Native boundary at which this selection takes effect.

ModelChangeEffect.description: The native harness boundary at which acknowledged settings affect work. This does not relabel an already running turn.

ModelChange.description: A model change in progress or awaiting recovery; the last confirmed model remains separate.

requestId.description: Correlated action identifier.

requestedModel.description: Exact model identifier within the conversation provider.

WorkspaceArrangement.description: How the window lays out its workspace, as chosen in Settings: three columns (sidebar, session list, panes), or sessions listed in the sidebar beside the panes.

WorkspaceShowing.description: What fills the window's content region: the panes, the Agents overview drawn over them, or a widget drawn over them.

WorkspaceWidget.description: A widget a pane or the window shows, by the plugin that draws it and its id within that plugin.

plugin.description: The plugin that draws the widget.

id.description: The widget's id within its plugin.

WorkspacePaneKind.description: What a pane shows: a conversation, a draft (a new conversation the person has not started yet), or a widget. Other kinds, such as an open file, are added here.

WorkspacePaneItem.description: What one pane shows. A conversation names its conversationId, a widget its widget, and a draft neither.

kind.description: What kind of thing the pane shows.

conversationId.description: Canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID of the conversation, when kind is conversation.

widget.description: The widget, when kind is widget.

WorkspacePane.description: One pane of a column, top to bottom.

heightPercent.description: The pane's share of its column's height, in whole percent.

focused.description: Whether this is the window's focused pane. At most one pane is.

WorkspaceColumn.description: One column of panes, left to right.

widthPercent.description: The column's share of the panes' width, in whole percent.

panes.description: The column's panes, top to bottom.

WorkspaceWindow.description: What one desktop window shows now: its arrangement, which side columns are drawn, what fills its content region, and its panes left to right, each column top to bottom. It names conversations by id only; their titles and agents are the gateway's to say.

sidebar.description: Whether the sidebar is drawn: open by the person's choice and not folded for room.

sessionList.description: Whether the session list column is drawn. The sidebar arrangement has none and always says false.

showing.description: What fills the content region now.

widget.description: The widget drawn over the panes, when showing is widget.

columns.description: The panes' columns, left to right.

ChannelErrorCode.description: Why the gateway refused a channel method. invalid_request: a name, notes, path or model that is not one a channel holds (a relative path, or resources past x-channelRules.maxResourceBytes, among them), or an agent this gateway has no runtime for. forbidden: the access policy does not let the caller make or list channels; a paired device never may. conversations_not_configured: this gateway runs no conversations. channel_folder_not_found: the chosen folder does not exist. channel_folder_not_a_directory: the chosen folder is a file. channel_folder_refused: the chosen folder is one agents must not work in: the root of a drive, a system folder or one that holds a system folder, the home folder or one that holds it, or the gateway's own data folder, one that holds it, or anything inside it other than a folder under its channels folder. channel_resource_not_found: a file or folder to attach does not exist. channel_limit_reached: the caller keeps the most channels a person may (x-channelRules.maxChannels). channel_request_conflict: the requestId already made another channel; nothing was made. channel_storage_unavailable: the channel or its folder could not be saved or made; nothing was kept. temporarily_unavailable: the gateway is busy or stopping; ask again.

Channel.description: One channel as a list names it: where its conversations' agents work and what a new conversation in it starts with (agent, model, approval preset). Its notes and resources are told to its agents and are not listed.

channelId.description: The channel's id: default for the default channel, else ch_ and ten base32 characters the gateway chose.

folder.description: The absolute folder its conversations' agents work in, resolved.

folderMade.description: The gateway made the folder, under its channels folder, because none was chosen. False for a chosen folder and for the default channel's.

agent.description: The agent a new conversation in the channel starts on; null for the default channel, whose new conversations start on whatever the surface picks.

model.description: The model a new conversation in the channel starts on; null for the default channel.

approvalMode.description: The preset a new conversation in the channel starts with; ask for the default channel.

createdAtMs.description: When the channel was made, in Unix milliseconds; 0 for the default channel.

ChannelCreateParams.description: Make a channel (channel.create). Repeating the same requestId with the same channel answers the channel it made; with another, channel_request_conflict. The folder is the one path a request may name, and only here: a conversation names its channel, never a folder.

requestId.description: Stable action identifier retained for retries of one logical command.

name.description: What the channel is called: trimmed, 1 to x-channelRules.maxNameChars characters, no control characters.

folder.description: An existing absolute folder the channel's agents work in. Omitted, the gateway makes one under its channels folder, named by the channel's id.

agent.description: The agent a new conversation in the channel starts on.

model.description: The model a new conversation in the channel starts on.

approvalMode.description: The preset a new conversation in the channel starts with; default ask.

notes.description: Notes every agent in the channel is told; omitted is none.

resources.description: Existing absolute files and folders to attach, none twice, at most x-channelRules.maxResourceBytes of paths in all; omitted is none.

ChannelCreateResult.description: The channel channel.create made, or made earlier under the same requestId.

ChannelListParams.description: Which page of the caller's channels to list (channel.list). Empty for the first.

after.description: The cursor an earlier page returned: list the channels made after that one. An id the caller has no channel under is refused invalid_request.

ChannelListResult.description: One page of the caller's channels (channel.list): the default channel first on the first page, then the rest in the order they were made.

channels.description: This page's channels, as many as fit one frame. Only the first page holds the default channel, and only when the gateway has a workspace.

complete.description: False when the frame bound left some out: the later ones made, listed from cursor.

cursor.description: Present exactly when complete is false: the last channel on this page, to send back as after for the next one.

WorkspacePublishParams.description: Tell the gateway what this connection's desktop window shows now (workspace.publish), so the person's agents can read it with the read_window tool. Each publication replaces this connection's previous one; one with a lower revision than the one held is not applied. A publication with no window withdraws it. The gateway keeps a window only while its connection is open: a closed connection withdraws it, and a window that connects again publishes again, under the same windowId, which replaces whatever an older connection of that window still holds.

windowId.description: The window's own id, made once when it opens and kept across its connections, so a connection it left behind never reads as a second window.

revision.description: The window's publication number, increasing with each change and kept across its connections.

window.description: What the window shows. Absent withdraws the window: it shows no workspace now.

WorkspacePublishResult.description: The answer to workspace.publish: the revision the gateway holds for this connection now, and whether this publication was applied.

revision.description: The revision held now: this one when applied, a later one when this one arrived after it.

applied.description: False when a later revision was already held, so this one changed nothing.
